name: Ivy style
summary: The dress of the American college man: an unpadded, natural-shouldered sack jacket, an oxford button-down shirt, chinos and flannels, worn with ease.

philosophy.core_thesis: A man's dress is plain, a little worn and made to last; it shows that he belongs and does not show that he tries.
design_principles: Cut the jacket on a straight sack line with a natural shoulder and no pad.
Use a 3-roll-2 front with a soft lapel, and a single vent at the back.
Wear an oxford cloth shirt with a button-down collar that rolls in a soft curve.
Pair the jacket with flannel grey trousers or cotton chinos with a plain front and a cuff of 4 cm.
Choose tweed, flannel or seersucker by the season, and cotton oxford in pale stripes.
Add a knit tie, a Shetland jumper or a repp-striped tie in two or three colours.
Keep shoes in brown leather with a thick sole, and let them age.
anti_patterns: A bold logo or a loud print

silhouette.shape: A straight, easy line from the shoulder to the hem, with no waist suppression.
silhouette.line: A soft, natural shoulder, a 3-roll-2 lapel, a straight trouser and a button-down collar.
silhouette.fit: Easy on the chest and the waist; the jacket hangs straight from the shoulder.
silhouette.proportion: Jacket length to the base of the thumb; lapel about 7 cm; trouser with a straight leg, a plain front and a 4 cm cuff.
rules: Leave the shoulder unpadded so that it follows the line of the body.
Roll the top button of the front so that the lapel curves in one line.
Mix a tweed jacket with grey flannel trousers, and a blue shirt with a plain tie.
Wear brown leather shoes, and let them show wear.
Keep colour in the tie, the sock and the shirt stripe.

fabrics.rule: Choose a natural cloth with a dry hand: oxford cotton for the shirt, chino twill for the trouser, and tweed or flannel for the jacket.

methods: back loop and a box pleat on the shirt
cinch strap at the back of the trousers
construction.closures: Three buttons with the top one rolled; a button-down collar; a plain fly with a button.
construction.details: A hook vent, a flap pocket, a patch pocket, a keeper loop on the shirt, and leather elbow patches on the jumper.

surface.pattern: Plain, or a stripe, check, madras plaid or a repp tie; tweed in muted herringbones.
surface.gloss: All cloth at 1–5 GU; the surface is dry and a little soft.
surface.wear: The style wants a worn look: a collar that frays, a jumper that is darned, a shoe that is scuffed.

palette.strategy: Muted greys, navy, olive and tan, with one bright accent in the tie or the sock.

processes: woven oxford cloth and chino twill by the mill
knit by the Shetland hand frame
wash and wear until the cloth softens
making.scale: Made in large runs by clothiers in New York and New England and sold at the campus shop; it was a plain, repeated uniform.
making.signs: A rolled lapel, a button-down collar, a natural shoulder and a back loop on the shirt.

pieces.form: Three-button sack jacket with a natural shoulder
Button-down shirt with a collar that rolls

canonical_works.work: The Man in the Gray Flannel Suit

evidence.title: President Kennedy at a Harvard-Columbia football game, 1963

emotion.target_response: A sense of ease and place: the viewer sees a plain, worn, well-made outfit and reads quiet confidence.

use_cases: a period costume brief for a 1950s campus or office
a menswear collection with a trad base
a fashion image prompt for a college quad
a study note on American menswear
avoid_when: the brief wants a sharp, slim, Italian cut
the brief is formal black tie
the brief wants technical or sports cloth

modifiers.how: Slim the jacket, shorten it, narrow the trouser, and add a strong stripe.
Pad and canvas the shoulder, cut a waist, and use a fine worsted.

ornament_level.note: The outfit is plain; a stripe, a plaid or a tie carries the colour.
